why: Guess conveys that recovery takes time and cannot be rushed, matching the can't-fix-overnight meaning despite the odd stock-refill phrasing.
Snowball icon and words convey a self-reinforcing loop growing on itself.
The grabbing CEO and worker read as wealth concentration rather than top-down micromanagement making a system brittle.
Guess captures the loss of self-organization but adds economic framing and misses the micromanagement cause.

Narration says balancing loops fix the monopoly runaway, but viewer reads draining the top with taxes, which is partly right yet the buckets omit the balancing-loop idea; mostly acceptable but frames it as drain not balance.
Viewer correctly sees more balancing policies being added to the list.
Meadows with a lever and the words convey paradigm change as the biggest lever and no paradigm being absolute truth.
Narration says paradigm change is hard because it needs millions to admit their worldview is wrong, but the dial and pass-a-bill suggest it is easy to tweak.
Mask and smirk with the words read as a polished excuse hiding bad behavior.
Viewer gets that we cannot perfectly control complex systems, matching the narration.
